transcript.user: I only want to understand how a vault deposit works. Do not prepare any transaction or ask for my financial profile.
transcript.content: A vault deposit is a transfer of your USDC into a smart-contract account that holds it for you. On MoonSafe's Arc vault, USDC is the network's native gas token, so the deposit is sent as native value in a single transaction that you sign in your own wallet. No separate "approve" step is needed, and the vault cannot move the money without your signature.

transcript.user: If I say "sounds good" to that explanation, does it mean a deposit was signed or money moved?
transcript.content: No. A "sounds good" from you is just a chat message. It does not sign anything and does not move any money. A deposit only happens when you approve a transaction in your own wallet, and nothing is sent until you do.

transcript.user: No deposit today. Explain testnet money versus money I can actually use for rent in one short paragraph.

Money you can actually use for rent is regular money in your bank account, or dollars you hold in a real currency or an exchange account you can withdraw to a bank. Keep real savings for real emergencies in that kind of accessible account, and use testnet only to try the app.

Approval happens only in your own wallet. A deposit is a transaction your wallet shows you, with the amount and destination, and it goes through only when you confirm it there.
